Categories.value: GFDL|Morris Marina|CC-BY-SA-3.0,2.5,2.0,1.0|License migration redundant|Self-published work|Automobiles in Vienna|1966 Morris automobiles|Photographs by Charles01

ImageDescription.value:
Morris Marina 2 door coupe shortly after model launch. During the 1974 fuel shortage, drivers in Austria found themselves barred from driving their car one day per week. The 'MI' sticker on the windscreen indicates that the driver may not drive his Vienna registered Marina 1.3 on a Wednesday (Mittwoch). The condensation on the screen indicates that the picture was taken on a cold though bright day.

Behind the Marina is a Ford Cortina Mk II. This is the Cortina version that was sold in the UK and in much of mainland Europe between 1966 and 1970: it is the competitor model that British Leyland had in their sights as they developed the Morris Marina.

In Austria, where the picture was taken, Volkswagen Beetles, like the one across the road, still dominated the market for small cars, though the Beetle was no longer quite the unstoppable sales success it had been a few years earlier: later in 1974 it was joined in the VW line-up by an interesting new model inspired by one Italian and designed by another.

ObjectName.value: Morris Minor van

Categories.value: Taken with Fujifilm FinePix F31fd|British Postal Museum & Archive|Flickr images reviewed by File Upload Bot (Magnus Manske)|1953 Morris vehicles|Royal Mail vans|Red Morris Minor vans

ImageDescription.value:
In 1953, the Morris Minor van was introduced as the standard small capacity mail van. It replaced the earlier Morris Series Z that had been used by The Post Office for small-scale deliveries. The first examples had a split windscreen, rubber front wings and high position headlamps.

A sturdy and reliable vehicle, the Morris Minor was held in high regard by postal workers. It remained the standard mail van for nearly twenty years. Production stopped in 1971 and the last Morris Minor van entered postal service the following year.

There were few small capacity vans on the market that the Post Office thought to be suitable replacements for the Morris Minor. A number of different types were tried out, including the Reliant three-wheeler, the Mini van, the Morris Marina and, what eventually became the standard small van used for a wide variety of duties, the Ford Escort.

However, none of these later replacements would hold the same place in people’s hearts and memories as that of the ‘little red van’ - the Morris Minor

For more information on this exhibition please visit: our website

ImageDescription.value:
Australian built Morris Marina Sedan. In 1973 the Australian Marina was renamed to Leyland Marina, given a facelift and offered with a 2620cc six cylinder engine option.

The Marinas were built in England from 1971-80, Australia 1972-75. With the British Leyland cars of this time, the Austins were front wheel drive cars and the Morris was rear wheel drive. ImageDescription.value:
The Morris Nomad was produced by Leyland Australia from 1969-72. It was a hatchback version of the Morris 1500 sedan. The first Australian built ADO16 was the 1964 Morris 1100. Updated in 1967 by the Morris S, with 1275cc engine. And again in 1969 by the Morris 1500, with a distinctive new front grille and 1500cc OHC engine from the UK Austin Maxi. The Nomad was released at the same time, even more like the Maxi with its hatchback.

Replaced in 1972 by the Morris Marina.

ObjectName.value: 1973 Leyland Marina 2 door Coupe (26292006332)

Categories.value: Morris Marina (Australia)|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Australia photographs taken on 2016-04-10|Photographs by Sicnag

ImageDescription.value:
Built in England from 1971-80, Australia 1972-75. With the British Leyland cars of this time, the Austins were front wheel drive cars and the Morris was rear wheel drive. Available in 1.3, 1.8 or twin carb TC 1.8 Also built by Leyland Australia from CKD kits from the UK, running gear was upgraded for the harsher conditions and a 6 cyl was also available. The Marina saw quite a few grille variations. The 1300 grille got chrome horizontal bars, with a central body coloured divider. Early 1800 grilles involved the painted horizontal body coloured bar. Later, the horizontal bar was filled with little chrome coloured horizontal bars. The 1800 TC - same engine with an extra carb - involved a slightly more elaborate horizontal painted bar, normally painted black, with TC written on it Some Australian and South African assembled cars had a grille with chrome vertical bars. Available in Saloon, Coupe, Pickup and Van.

Engines; 1500 and 1750 4 cyl or 2600 6 cyl
